children.text:
开场 1：你在埃纳尔旅店过夜。你的休息一点也不安宁。即便有人能在梦中入睡，你也绝对睡不着。你的脑中满是即将到来的任务带来的焦虑。你回想黑猫关于清醒世界危险的警告，又想起那些跟随维吉尔·格雷走下沉睡的阶梯、穿过魔幻森林的人。他们现在也在这里吗？也许只要找到那座城堡，带着幻梦境的证据回去，你就能救下所有人：你自己、你的朋友，以及其他入梦者。

查看战役日志。

• 如果「黑猫在你身边」，前往〈开场 2〉。

• 如果上述条件不成立，且卢克·罗宾逊在这个团队中，跳过，直接前往〈开场 3〉。

• 如果以上两种情况都不成立，跳过，直接前往〈开场 4〉。

开场 2：天亮时，光线从你房间的窗帘缝隙透进来，你注意到窗前坐着一个猫形的剪影。等视线适应后，你被它那双锐利的黄色眼睛钉在原地，那眼睛亮得像晨光。你认出这个身影就是维吉尔会说话的那只猫。你问黑猫在那里坐了多久。

“够久了，久到能看出你既不在清醒，也不在沉睡。”它自相矛盾地回答。

这个世界的本质仍然让你困惑。人在幻梦境里也能睡觉吗？如果能，他们的心智又会去哪里？出于好奇，你向猫提出了这个问题。

“以肉身来到这里的人可以睡，但你完全是另一回事。好了，别再想这些了，谈正事。”黑猫跳上你的床。“你要我带的话，我已经把警告带给你那些朋友了。看来他们也正准备进入幻梦境。这期间我会跟着你。反正总得有人看着你和我养的那个人类。”

查看战役日志。

• 如果卢克·罗宾逊在这个团队中，前往〈开场 3〉。

• 否则，跳过，直接前往〈开场 4〉。

开场 3：早晨，你发现维吉尔和伦道夫在埃纳尔旅店外的市镇广场上谈话。你仍说不准该怎么看待他们两人，但你很清楚接下来该往哪里去。毕竟，这已不是你第一次踏入传说中的幻梦境。你转向伦道夫，提议去附近的长老神庙找高阶祭司阿塔尔谈谈。这是你上一次在睡梦中造访乌撒时听过的名字，只是此前你没有理由去寻求这位祭司的建议。伦道夫惊讶地瞥了你一眼，随即露出一丝得意的笑。

“真巧，”他说，“我正想提同样的建议。阿塔尔的智慧远在我们所有人的估量之上。他也许知道该去哪里找我们要找的地方。”

维吉尔急着开始这场冒险，拍了拍手。“那还等什么？这边走，朋友们！”

你点点头，朝神庙走去。那是一座象牙色的圆形石塔，盘踞在镇中最高的小山之上。一小队猫在墙边巡逻。队伍最前方的那只猫，正是你们先前在树林里遇到的、身上带疤的老猫。它上前一步挡住入口，满怀敌意地打量着你们一行人。

“又见面了，”老猫语气尖刻地说，“我猜你们想让我让开。”

查看战役日志。

• 如果调查员和祖格鼠谈判过，或调查员被伦道夫·卡特救下，跳过，直接前往〈开场 5〉。

• 如果猫群收到了祖格鼠的贡品，跳过，直接前往〈开场 6〉。

开场 4：第二天早晨，你发现维吉尔和伦道夫在埃纳尔旅店外的市镇广场上谈话。虽然你还说不准该怎么看待他们两人，但你知道他们都十分熟悉这片奇异土地的形势。你问他们下一步该怎么做。“我们该去长老神庙找高阶祭司阿塔尔谈谈，”伦道夫提议，“他的智慧远在我们所有人的估量之上，也许知道该去哪里找我们要找的地方。”你出声问道，神庙离这里有多远。

“一点也不远，”伦道夫回答，“它就立在乌撒最高的那座小山顶上。来吧，我带路。”由伦道夫领头，你们前往长老神庙。那是一座象牙色的圆形石塔，由一小队猫守卫着。队伍最前方的那只猫，正是你们先前在树林里遇到的、身上带疤的老猫。它上前一步挡住入口，满怀敌意地打量着你们一行人。

“又见面了，”老猫语气尖刻地说，“我猜你们想让我让开。”

查看战役日志。

• 如果调查员和祖格鼠谈判过，或调查员被伦道夫·卡特救下，前往〈开场 5〉。

• 如果猫群收到了祖格鼠的贡品，跳过，直接前往〈开场 6〉。

开场 5：“那可真不巧，”猫说着，尾巴绷得笔直。更多的猫从两侧包抄上来，好几只大声嘶叫。它们的毛炸开，眼里燃起怒火。“看守这里、不让你们这种莽撞的外来者闯入，是我们的职责。这里不欢迎你们。”

“讲讲道理，”伦道夫恳求道，“我们只是想来和阿塔尔谈谈。我们没有恶意。”

“嘴上说一套，手上做一套。”疤脸猫来回踱步。“现在滚出去，别再回来。”

调查员必须决定（选择一项）：

• 空手离开。跳过，直接前往〈开场 7〉。

• 强行闯入神庙。跳过，直接前往〈开场 8〉。

开场 6：你告诉猫，你只是来和阿塔尔谈谈，并无恶意。“啊，别担心，人类，”猫张大嘴打了个哈欠——那种只有猫才能打得又保持威严的哈欠。“你看起来不像会惹麻烦的那种人。再说，我哪也不打算去。”你看见猫面前有个小小的隆起：一只带血、被吃掉一半的野鸡。你忍住皱鼻子的冲动，庆幸自己站在这只猫的这一边。“进去吧。”它说着舔了舔嘴，准备把饭吃完。

跳过，直接前往〈开场 9〉。

开场 7：你无奈地离开山顶的神庙。“看来我们只能在没有阿塔尔指点的情况下想办法了，”伦道夫叹着气说，“无论如何，我们的目的地很可能远在此处之外——甚至可能在另一块大陆上。我们得设法搭船。我建议南下，去港口城市狄拉斯-利恩。到了那里我们再想下一步。”你点点头，最后看了一眼那座石制神庙，想着自己或许就此错失了怎样的知识。

跳过，直接前往〈设置〉。

开场 8：你告诉猫，无论用什么办法你都要进神庙，一只普通的猫挡不住你。“想赌一把？”它低吼着压低身子，准备扑上来。几只守着神庙的猫注意到动静，围了上来。你不想伤害这些猫，但也不会让它们挡住你的目标。你向同伴点头示意，朝神庙大门猛冲。嘶声与愤怒的尖啸在你四周爆发，猫群拼死防守。一堵由小爪子和尖牙组成的墙迎面扑来，你仍然顶了过去。你反手把石门重重关上，听见老猫在另一侧大喊：“行啊，人类！去见你的祭司吧！但别以为这次冒犯会被原谅！”

• 在你的战役日志中记录「调查员强行进入神庙」。

前往〈开场 9〉。

开场 9：神庙顶端，高阶祭司阿塔尔坐在象牙色的高台上等你们。他是个瘦削虚弱的老人，留着长而稀疏的黑胡子，双颊凹陷，眼睛苍白浑浊，像是失明的人。“别被自己的眼睛骗了，”你们在高台前落座时，伦道夫低声说，“阿塔尔已经活了三百多年，可他的记性好得很。”

你向祭司问起你的任务和目的地：伦道夫在梦里描述的那座城堡。“你说的是伟大的存在安息的地方，高踞于未知的卡达斯之上。连我也不知道它的确切位置。这倒也好，因为妄图登上那种地方，结出的果实必定苦涩。我的同伴巴尔扎伊曾攀上一座远不及那里神圣的山峰，从此再没人见过他，也没人听过他的消息。卡达斯的神明或许看似无力，但他们受外神庇护，那些外神还是不要谈论为好。对一切神明敬而远之，把这桩蠢事抛在身后，才是更明智的做法。”

阿塔尔用了“神明”这个词，让你很好奇。你出声问道，这种地方会住着什么样的神明。

祭司摇摇头。“他们不是我们的神明，而是地球的神明，因为这片土地不过是你们那个世界的倒影。”

你试图继续追问，想从阿塔尔口中挖出更多智慧，但他的态度毫不动摇。“我已经说得太多了，”他坚持道，“求你了，为了你自己好，别再追寻这种疯狂。”

• 在你的战役日志中，在「卡达斯的证据」旁记录 1 个计数标记。

查看战役日志。

• 如果调查员和祖格鼠谈判过，前往〈开场 10〉。

• 如果猫群收到了祖格鼠的贡品，或调查员被伦道夫·卡特救下，跳过，直接前往〈开场 11〉。

开场 10：灵光一闪，你想起祖格鼠在魔幻森林里送给你的月酒。你拿出一些献给阿塔尔，他欣然接受。你假装自己也喝了，却一杯接一杯地给祭司斟上。终于，阿塔尔的嘴松了，他开始讲那些若没有酒绝不会提起的禁忌之事。他讲到奥瑞巴岛上恩格拉尼克山的山面刻着一幅画像——据他说，那是众神的容貌。他讲到卡达瑟隆的柱子，地球幻梦境的历史就记载在那里。他讲到那些被黑夜本身的军团杀死、葬在死者之城祖兰-提克地穴里的人。他讲到一座地图上从未出现的被遗忘之城上空那颗凶星。“如果你非要到冰封荒土里去找卡达斯，”他昏昏欲睡地说，“南边沿海有座城市：狄拉斯-利恩。你可以在那里设法搭船。”

• 在你的战役日志中，在「卡达斯的证据」旁记录 1 个计数标记。

• 每名调查员获得 2 点经验。

跳过，直接前往〈设置〉。

开场 11：阿塔尔拒绝再给你任何建议，于是你决定离开山顶的神庙。“我们学到了很多，可离知道卡达斯的位置还是没近多少，”伦道夫叹着气说，“我们的目的地很可能远在此处之外——甚至可能在另一块大陆上。要走这么远的路，我们得设法搭船。我建议先南下，去港口城市狄拉斯-利恩。到了那里我们再想下一步。”

前往〈设置〉。
从以下遭遇组收集所有卡牌：寻觅卡达斯、奈亚拉托提普的使徒、海盗、幻梦境、修普诺斯的低语与祖格鼠。
将乌撒、斯凯河与狄拉斯-利恩放入场中。
每名调查员从乌撒开始游戏。
将其他每个地点放在一边，置于场外。
将以下敌人放在一边，置于场外：乌撒之猫、跟踪的蝎狮、蠕行之雾、夜色怪群、伊伯生物、两张黑暗夜魇、两张冷原海盗，以及全部 3 张千面祭司。
在已收集的遭遇卡中找出 1 张一群乌尼斯，并将其生成在斯凯河。如果游戏中有 3 或 4 名调查员，则在已收集的遭遇卡中再找出 1 张一群乌尼斯，并将其生成在狄拉斯-利恩。
队长取得维吉尔·格雷（怪谈作家）剧情支援的控制权，并将其放入场中。
将剩余的遭遇卡混洗，组建遭遇牌库。
每名调查员失去其所有的线索。
将场上的每个地点移出游戏（如果该地点有胜利 X 且其上没有线索，则改为将其放入胜利区）。那些地点上的每个敌人和附属均被弃掉。此过程不会使调查员被击败。
将每个放在一边的奥瑞巴地点放入场中（巴哈那港、恩格拉尼克山脉与无名遗迹）。
将每名调查员放置在巴哈那港。
在遭遇牌库中找出 1 张夜骑，并将其生成在恩格拉尼克山脉。如果游戏中有 3 或 4 名调查员，则在遭遇牌库中再找出 1 张夜骑，并将其生成在无名遗迹。混洗遭遇牌库。
推进到幕 2a——“奥瑞巴岛”。
每名调查员失去其所有的线索。
将场上的每个地点移出游戏（如果该地点有胜利 X 且其上没有线索，则改为将其放入胜利区）。那些地点上的每个敌人和附属均被弃掉。此过程不会使调查员被击败。
将每个放在一边的米纳尔地点放入场中（卡达瑟隆、萨尔纳斯与伊伯遗迹）。
将每名调查员放置在卡达瑟隆。
将放在一边的伊伯生物敌人生成在伊伯遗迹。
推进到幕 2a——“昔日厄运”。
每名调查员失去其所有的线索。
将场上的每个地点移出游戏（如果该地点有胜利 X 且其上没有线索，则改为将其放入胜利区）。那些地点上的每个敌人和附属均被弃掉。此过程不会使调查员被击败。
将放在一边的禁闭之地各地点放入场中（伊莱克-瓦达、禁闭之地与祖兰-提克）。
将每名调查员放置在伊莱克-瓦达。
将放在一边的跟踪的蝎狮敌人生成在禁闭之地。
将放在一边的夜色怪群敌人生成在祖兰-提克。
推进到幕 2a——“找寻黑夜”。
每名调查员失去其所有的线索。
将场上的每个地点移出游戏（如果该地点有胜利 X 且其上没有线索，则改为将其放入胜利区）。那些地点上的每个敌人和附属均被弃掉。此过程不会使调查员被击败。
将塞勒菲斯、塞拉尼安与哈祖斯-克列格放入场中。
将每名调查员放置在塞勒菲斯。
将放在一边的蠕行之雾混洗入遭遇牌库。
在遭遇牌库中找出 1 张千面祭司，并将其生成在哈祖斯-克列格。如果游戏中有 3 或 4 名调查员，则在遭遇牌库中再找出 1 张千面祭司，并将其生成在塞勒菲斯。混洗遭遇牌库。
推进到幕 2a——“王之判决”。

本剧本中的每个地点都没有未揭示面，因此它们以已揭示面朝上的方式进入场中。这些地点的背面放的是剧情卡，而不是未揭示面。每当本剧本中的某个地点进入场中（包括在设置期间），都照常在该地点上放置等同于其线索值的线索。

地点可以通过以下两种方式之一翻面。大多数地点由掩藏关键词翻面，详见下文。少数地点则由印在该地点上的能力翻面。

一旦某个地点翻面、其剧情文本被读过，除非另有说明，否则在本局游戏的剩余时间内它不能再翻面。

本剧本中的许多地点具有掩藏关键词。该关键词表示该地点含有未知的学识或援助，调查员必须先将其找出来，它才能为他们所用。

作为一项 [fast] 能力，位于某个没有线索的掩藏地点的调查员可以将该地点翻面，并结算其另一面的文本。

children.title: 具有蜂拥与胜利的敌人

children.text: 当胜利 X 出现在某个蜂拥敌人上时，该文本仅对头领卡有效。蜂拥卡牌不能进入胜利区，也永远不计胜利点。

本关的地点没有未揭示面，入场时以揭示面朝上放置。它们的背面是剧情卡。每当本关的地点入场（包括设置时），照常放置等于其线索值的线索。

地点可以通过两种方式翻面：大部分通过下述“帷幕”关键词翻面，某些则通过印在地点上的能力翻面。

除非另有说明，一个地点翻面且其剧情文字被阅读后，本局剩余时间不能再次翻面。

本关的许多地点具有“帷幕”关键词，表示其中隐藏着未知的知识或援助，需要调查员先行探寻才能利用。

作为一个 [free] 能力，位于没有线索的帷幕地点的调查员可以将该地点翻面，结算另一面的文字。

children.title: 具有集群和胜利点的敌人

children.text: 当一个集群敌人印有“胜利 X”时，该文字只对宿主卡生效。集群卡不能进入胜利牌区，也永远不提供胜利点数。

在结算任何其他结局之前，如果至少有 1 名调查员被击败：被击败的调查员先阅读〈调查员落败〉。

调查员落败：你醒来时发现自己被粗麻绳捆着，躺在坚硬潮湿的木板上。地板来回摇晃，你听见海浪拍打舱壁。你被囚禁在一艘帆船上。可为什么？

• 在你的战役日志中，每名被击败的调查员记录「（你的调查员名）被俘」。

• 如果某名被击败的调查员的牌库中有伦道夫·卡特，且至少有 1 名调查员撤退，则将伦道夫·卡特的所有权交给一名已撤退的调查员。

• 前往调查员达成的结局。如果没有达成结局……

• ……且有至少 1 名调查员撤退，前往〈结局 1〉。

• ……且每名调查员都被击败，跳过，直接前往〈结局 2〉。

如果没有达成结局：

• 如果至少有 1 名调查员撤退，前往〈结局 1〉。

• 如果每名调查员都被击败，跳过，直接前往〈结局 2〉。

结局 1（每名被击败的调查员应先结算〈调查员落败〉）：你走遍了远近各地，从斯凯王国铺着鹅卵石的古朴村庄，到百年之间你也想象不到的奇妙土地。你对幻梦境，以及居住在未知的卡达斯之上的神明，了解了许多。虽然你离目标更近了，却仍不知道它的确切位置。与此同时，你的任务一天比一天凶险。无论你走到哪里，都有污秽可怖的生物跨陆越海地追赶你。没有面孔的带翼野兽，手持锋利弯刀、指挥着巨大黑色帆船的长角海盗——这些夺命的爪牙形貌各异。你决定回到船上，远离幻梦境的种种危险……至少你是这么想的。

不幸的是，你的船并不是安全的避风港。你回到船上时，船员和船长都不见了踪影。船上没有打斗的痕迹，但先前回船准备下一次启航的维吉尔也失踪了。

“我担心是最坏的情况，”伦道夫悲叹道，“如果那些凶残的海盗抓了他们，他们就危险了。那些海盗是外神的爪牙，而外神的灵魂与使者，就是蠕行之混沌奈亚拉托提普。”光是说出这个名字，就让你不寒而栗，尽管你并不知道为什么。你问他们可能被带去了哪里。他像是在谈论又一个停靠港似的答道：“那些驱使黑色帆船的野兽从月亮启航。要救回维吉尔和其他同伴，我们就得去那里。”

• 每名调查员获得经验，数值等于胜利区中每张卡牌的胜利 X 值。

• 调查员在本剧本中每发现一个神迹，就在战役日志中「卡达斯的证据」旁记录 1 个计数标记。

• 在你的战役日志中记录「维吉尔被俘」。

• 在你的战役日志中记录「伦道夫未遭俘虏」。

• 如果你以互联的八章战役形式同时进行梦寻与梦网……

• ……且尚未进行〈剧本 2–B：万千骇形〉，前往该剧本。

• ……且已经进行过〈剧本 2–B：万千骇形〉，改为前往〈幕间 II：入梦者〉。

结局 2：你打量四周，发现维吉尔和伦道夫等其他同伴也都被俘了。他们此刻昏迷不醒，但也许等他们醒来，你们就能想出一个脱身的计划。毕竟，尽管遭遇了这次挫折，你对幻梦境，以及居住在未知的卡达斯之上的神明，已经了解了许多。虽然你仍不知道它的确切位置，但只要能逃出这艘破船，你的任务或许还有希望。你咽下一团绝望，希望这还不是旅程的终点……

Intro 1: You stay the night at Einar’s Place. Your rest is anything but peaceful. Even if one could sleep within a dream, you certainly do not. Your mind teems with anxiety over the quest looming ahead. You reflect on the black cat’s warning about danger in the waking world, and you wonder about the others who have followed Virgil Gray down the steps of slumber and through the Enchanted Woods. Are they here now, too? Perhaps if you find this castle and return with proof of the Dreamlands, you can save everyone: yourself, your friends, and the other dreamers as well.

Check Campaign Log.

• If the black cat is at your side, proceed to Intro 2.

• If the above is not true, and Luke Robinson is in this group, skip to Intro 3.

• If neither of the above is true, skip to Intro 4.

Intro 2: When day breaks and light peeks through the curtains of your room, you notice a cat-shaped silhouette sitting in front of the window. As your vision adjusts, you are transfixed by its piercing yellow eyes, bright as the dawn light. You recognize the shape as Virgil’s talking cat. You ask the black cat how long it has been sitting there.

“Long enough to know you are neither waking nor asleep,” it replies paradoxically.

The nature of this world still confounds you. Can one even sleep in the Dreamlands? If so, where would their minds go? Curious, you pose this question to the cat.

“Those here in their physical bodies can, but you are something else entirely. Now, never mind all that. On to business.” The black cat leaps onto your bed. “I gave your friends the warning you wanted me to pass along. They are preparing to enter the Dreamlands as well, it seems. In the meantime, I will stay with you. Somebody has to watch over you and my pet human, anyway.”

Check Campaign Log.

• If Luke Robinson is in this group, proceed to Intro 3.

• Otherwise, skip to Intro 4.

Intro 3: In the morning, you find Virgil and Randolph talking in the town square outside of Einar’s Place. You still aren’t quite sure what to think of either of them, but you have a good sense of where you should go next. After all, this is not your first excursion into the fabled land of dreams. Addressing Randolph, you suggest talking to the high priest Atal in the nearby Temple of the Elder Ones. It is a name you heard the last time you visited the city of Ulthar in your sleep, though until now you had no reason to seek the priest’s advice. Randolph gives you a startled glance that transforms quickly into a smirk.

“How curious,” he says, “I was about to suggest the same. Atal is wise beyond all our measure. He may know where to find the place we seek.”

Virgil, eager to embark on this adventure, claps his hands. “Well, what are we waiting for? This way, my friends!”

You nod and head for the temple, a circular tower of ivoried stone crowning the highest hill in town. A small army of cats patrols its walls. The cat at the head of the formation is none other than the old cat with the scar you encountered in the woods earlier. He steps forward to bar your entry and regards your party with great acrimony.

“Hello again,” the old cat says with a sharp tone. “I suppose yeh want me to step aside.”

Check Campaign Log.

• If the investigators parleyed with the Zoogs, or if the investigators were saved by Randolph Carter, skip to Intro 5.

• If the cats collected their tribute from the Zoogs, skip to Intro 6.

Intro 4: The next morning, you find Virgil and Randolph talking in the town square outside of Einar’s Place. Though you aren’t quite sure what to think of either of them just yet, you know that both of them are well versed in the lay of this strange land. You ask them about your next move. “We should speak to the high priest Atal in the Temple of the Elder Ones,” Randolph suggests. “He is wise beyond all our measure and may know where to find the place we seek.” You wonder aloud how far the temple is from here.

“Not far at all,” Randolph replies. “It stands atop the highest hill within Ulthar. Come, I will lead the way.” With Randolph taking the lead, you make your way to the Temple of the Elder Ones, a circular tower of ivoried stone protected by a small army of cats. The cat at the head of the formation is none other than the old cat with the scar you encountered in the woods earlier. He steps forward to bar your entry and regards your party with great acrimony.

“Hello again,” the old cat says with a sharp tone. “I suppose yeh want me to step aside.”

Check Campaign Log.

• If the investigators parleyed with the Zoogs, or if the investigators were saved by Randolph Carter, proceed to Intro 5.

• If the cats collected their tribute from the Zoogs, skip to Intro 6.

Intro 5: “Well, too bad,” the cat says, tail stiff and straight. More cats flank you from the sides, several hissing loudly. Their fur puffs up, and their eyes flare with anger. “It’s our duty to guard this place from impetuous outsiders like yerself. Yeh ain’t wanted here.”

“Be reasonable,” Randolph implores. “We are only trying to speak with Atal. We mean no harm.”

“Yeh can mean one thing and do another.” The scarred cat paces. “Now get outta here and don’t come back.”

The investigators must decide (choose one):

• Leave empty-handed. Skip to Intro 7.

• Force your way into the temple. Skip to Intro 8.

Intro 6: You tell the cat that you are merely here to speak with Atal, and that you mean no harm. “Ah, no worries, human,” the cat says with a gaping yawn—the kind only a cat can perform and still look regal in the act. “You don’t seem the type to make trouble. ’Sides, I ain’t goin’ nowhere.” You see a small lump in front of the cat: a bloodied, half-eaten pheasant. You resist the urge to turn up your nose and count yourself lucky you are on this cat’s good side. “Go on in,” he says, then licks his chops as he prepares to finish his meal.

Skip to Intro 9.

Intro 7: Resigned, you leave the temple on the hilltop behind. “I suppose we shall have to make do without Atal’s wisdom,” Randolph says with a sigh. “In any event, it is likely our destination is far from here—perhaps on another continent altogether. We will need to secure passage by sea. I suggest we travel south, to the port city of Dylath‑Leen. We can figure out our next step from there.” You nod and take one last look at the stone temple, wondering at the knowledge you may have left behind.

Skip to Setup.

Intro 8: You inform the cat you are entering the temple one way or another, and that a simple cat will not stand in your way. “Wanna bet?” he growls, lowering his body and preparing to pounce. Noticing the commotion, several cats guarding the temple surround you. You don’t wish to harm these cats, but you won’t let them block you from your objective, either. Nodding to your companions, you make a mad dash for the temple gates. A storm of hisses and angry screeches erupts all around you as the cats mount a desperate defense. A wall of tiny claws and teeth meets you, but you push through, defiant. You slam the stone door shut behind you and hear the old cat yelling from the other side: “Fine then, human! See your priest! But do not think this transgression will be forgiven!”

• In your Campaign Log, record the investigators forced their way into the temple.

Proceed to Intro 9.

Intro 9: At the top of the temple, seated on an ivory dais, the high priest Atal awaits you. He is a frail, wiry man with a long, wispy black beard, caved-in cheeks, and the pale, milky eyes of one afflicted by blindness. “Do not let your eyes deceive you,” Randolph whispers as you seat yourselves in front of the dais. “Atal is over three centuries old, but his memory is sharp as a tack.”

You ask the priest about your quest and about your destination: the castle Randolph described from his dreams. “You speak of the resting place of the Great Ones, high above unknown Kadath. Even I know not its true location. And that is all well and good, for the fruits of attempting to ascend to such a place would be bitter indeed. My companion Barzai once scaled a peak only a fraction as sacred, and he was never seen nor heard from again. The gods of Kadath may seem powerless, but they are protected by the Other Gods from the Outside, whom it is better not to discuss. It would be wiser to let all the gods alone and leave this folly behind.”

Atal’s use of the word “gods” has you curious. You wonder aloud what kind of god might exist in a place like this.

The priest shakes his head. “They are not our gods, but the gods of Earth, for this land is but a reflection of yours.”

You attempt to pry deeper into Atal’s wisdom with your questioning, but his advice does not budge. “I have already said more than I should,” he insists. “Please, for your sake, pursue this madness no further.”

• In your Campaign Log, next to “Evidence of Kadath,” record 1 tally mark.

Check Campaign Log.

• If the investigators parleyed with the Zoogs, proceed to Intro 10.

• If the cats collected their tribute from the Zoogs, or if the investigators were saved by Randolph Carter, skip to Intro 11.

Intro 10: A flash of inspiration strikes you, and you remember the moon-wine given to you by the Zoogs in the Enchanted Woods. You offer some to Atal, and he accepts graciously. You pretend to partake of the wine yourself while offering draught after draught to the priest. Eventually, Atal’s lips loosen, and he speaks of forbidden things he would never discuss were it not for the wine. He tells of an image carved into the face of the mountain Ngranek on the isle of Oriab—the likeness of the gods, or so he claims. He tells of the pillars of Kadatheron wherein the history of Earth’s Dreamlands is recorded. He tells of those slain by the hordes of Night itself and interred in the crypts of Zulan-Thek, the city of the dead. He tells of a baleful star above a forgotten city that appears on no map. “If you absolutely must seek Kadath in the Cold Wastes,” he says drowsily, “there is a city along the coast to the south: Dylath-Leen. You may secure passage there.”

• In your Campaign Log, next to “Evidence of Kadath,” record 1 tally mark.

• Each investigator earns 2 experience.

Skip to Setup.

Intro 11: Atal refuses to give you any more advice, so you decide to leave the temple on the hilltop behind. “We have learned much, but we are still no closer to knowing the location of Kadath,” Randolph says with a sigh. “It is likely that our destination is far from here—perhaps on another continent altogether. We shall need to secure passage by sea if we are to travel such great distances. I suggest we begin by traveling south, to the port city of Dylath‑Leen. We can figure out our next step from there.”

Proceed to Setup.
Gather all cards from the following encounter sets: The Search for Kadath, Agents of Nyarlathotep, Corsairs, Dreamlands, Whispers of Hypnos, and Zoogs.
Put Ulthar, Skai River, and Dylath-Leen into play.
Each investigator begins play in Ulthar.
Set each other location aside, out of play.

Set the following enemies aside, out of play: Cats of Ulthar, Stalking Manticore, The Crawling Mist, Horde of Night, Beings of Ib, both copies of Tenebrous Nightgaunt, both copies of Corsair of Leng, and all 3 copies of Priest of a Thousand Masks.

Search the gathered encounter cards for 1 copy of Pack of Vooniths and spawn it at Skai River. If there are 3 or 4 investigators in the game, search the gathered encounter cards for another copy of Pack of Vooniths and spawn it at Dylath-Leen, as well.
The lead investigator takes control of the Virgil Gray (Writer of Strange Tales) story asset and puts him into play.
Shuffle the remainder of the encounter cards to build the encounter deck.
Each investigator loses each of their clues.

Remove each location in play from the game (or place it in the victory display if it has Victory X and no clues on it). Each enemy and attachment at those locations is discarded. Investigators are not defeated during this process.
Put each set-aside Oriab location into play (Baharna, Mt. Ngranek, and Nameless Ruins).
Place each investigator at Baharna.

Search the encounter deck for 1 copy of Nightriders and spawn it at Mt. Ngranek. If there are 3 or 4 investigators in the game, search the encounter deck for another copy of Nightriders and spawn it at Nameless Ruins, as well. Shuffle the encounter deck.
Advance to Act 2a—“The Isle of Oriab.”
Each investigator loses each of their clues.

Remove each location in play from the game (or place it in the victory display if it has Victory X and no clues on it). Each enemy and attachment at those locations is discarded. Investigators are not defeated during this process.
Put each set-aside Mnar location into play (Kadatheron, Sarnath, and Ruins of Ib).
Place each investigator at Kadatheron.
Spawn the set-aside Beings of Ib enemy at Ruins of Ib.
Advance to Act 2a—“The Doom That Came Before.”
Each investigator loses each of their clues.

Remove each location in play from the game (or place it in the victory display if it has Victory X and no clues on it). Each enemy and attachment at those locations is discarded. Investigators are not defeated during this process.
Put each set-aside Forbidden location into play (Ilek-Vad, Forbidden Lands, and Zulan-Thek).
Place each investigator at Ilek-Vad.
Spawn the set-aside Stalking Manticore enemy at Forbidden Lands.
Spawn the set-aside Horde of Night enemy at Zulan-Thek.
Advance to Act 2a—“Seek Out the Night.”
Each investigator loses each of their clues.

Remove each location in play from the game (or place it in the victory display if it has Victory X and no clues on it). Each enemy and attachment at those locations is discarded. Investigators are not defeated during this process.
Put Celephaïs, Serannian, and Hazuth-Kleg into play.
Place each investigator at Celephaïs.
Shuffle the set-aside The Crawling Mist into the encounter deck.

Search the encounter deck for 1 copy of Priest of a Thousand Masks and spawn it at Hazuth-Kleg. If there are 3 or 4 investigators in the game, search the encounter deck for another copy of Priest of a Thousand Masks and spawn it at Celephaïs, as well. Shuffle the encounter deck.
Advance to Act 2a—“The King’s Decree.”

children.title: Locations in The Search for Kadath

children.text:
Each of the locations in this scenario have no unrevealed side, and therefore they enter play with their revealed side faceup. Instead of an unrevealed side, these locations have story cards on their reverse sides. Whenever a location in this scenario enters play (including during setup), place clues on that location equal to its clue value, as normal.

Locations can be flipped over in one of two ways. Most are flipped over by the veiled keyword, as described below. Some locations are instead flipped over by an ability printed on that location.

Once a location has been flipped over and its story text has been read, it cannot be flipped over again for the remainder of the game unless otherwise noted.

Many of the locations in this scenario have the veiled keyword. This keyword represents that a location contains unknown lore or assistance that must be sought out by the investigators before it can be of use to them.

As a [free] ability, an investigator at a veiled location with no clues on it may flip that location over, resolving the text on its other side.
When Victory X appears on a swarming enemy, this text is only active for the host card. Swarm cards cannot enter the victory display and are never worth victory points.

Before resolving any other resolution, if at least one investigator was defeated: The defeated investigators read Investigator Defeat first.

Investigator Defeat: You wake to find yourself restrained by thick cords of hempen rope, lying on top of hard, moist wood. The floor rocks steadily back and forth, and you hear ocean waves crashing against the walls. You are captive aboard some kind of galley. But why?

• In your Campaign Log, each defeated investigator records (your investigator name) was captured.

• If a defeated investigator’s deck contains Randolph Carter and at least 1 investigator resigned, give ownership of Randolph Carter to an investigator who resigned.

• Proceed to the resolution the investigators reached. If no resolution was reached…
• …and at least 1 investigator resigned, proceed to Resolution 1.

• …and each investigator was defeated, skip to Resolution 2.

If no resolution was reached:

• If at least 1 investigator resigned, proceed to Resolution 1.

• If each investigator was defeated, skip to Resolution 2.

Resolution 1 (each defeated investigator should resolve Investigator Defeat first): You have ventured far and wide, from the quaint cobbled villages of the kingdom of the Skai to wondrous lands you could have never in a hundred years imagined. You learned much of the Dreamlands and of the gods who dwell atop unknown Kadath. Though you are closer to your goal, you still don’t know its precise location. In the meantime, your quest grows deadlier with each passing day. No matter where you go, foul, nightmarish creatures pursue you across land and sea. Winged beasts with no faces, horned Corsairs wielding razor-sharp cutlasses and commanding great black galleys—the agents of your demise bear many shapes. You decide to return to your ship, safe from the many dangers of the Dreamlands…or so you thought.

Unfortunately, your ship is no safe haven. When you return, the crew and captain are nowhere to be found. There are no signs of struggle, but Virgil, who returned to the ship earlier to prepare for your next departure, is also missing.

“I fear the worst,” Randolph mourns. “If those fiendish Corsairs captured them, they are in dire trouble. They are agents of the Other Gods from the Outside, whose soul and messenger is the crawling chaos Nyarlathotep.” The mere utterance of the name causes you to shudder, though you do not know why. You ask where they might have been taken. As if discussing any other port of call, he replies: “The beasts who command their black galleys sail from the Moon. If we are to rescue Virgil and our other companions, that is where we must go.”

• Each investigator earns experience equal to the Victory X value of each card in the victory display.

• For each Sign of the Gods the investigators unveiled during this scenario, record 1 tally mark next to “Evidence of Kadath” in your Campaign Log.

• In your Campaign Log, record Virgil was captured.

• In your Campaign Log, record Randolph eluded capture.

• If you are playing The Dream-Quest as a four-part campaign, proceed to Scenario 3–A: Dark Side of the Moon.

• If you are playing The Dream-Quest and The Web of Dreams as an interconnected eight-part campaign…
• …and you have not yet played Scenario 2–B: A Thousand Shapes of Horror, proceed to that scenario.

• …and you have already played Scenario 2–B: A Thousand Shapes of Horror, proceed instead to Interlude II: The Oneironauts.

Resolution 2: As you examine your surroundings, you notice that your other companions, including Virgil and Randolph, have been captured as well. They are unconscious at the moment, but maybe when they awaken you can formulate a plan to free yourselves. After all, despite this setback, you have learned much of the Dreamlands and of the gods who dwell atop unknown Kadath. Though you still don’t know its precise location, if you are able to escape from this wretched galley, perhaps there is hope for your quest. You swallow a ball of despair and hope that this is not the end of your journey…

• Each investigator earns experience equal to the Victory X value of each card in the victory display.
